chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Uthman went out as a pilgrim, and when he reached al-Abwa', he ordered a crier to announce to the people: 'Make it a single Hajj (Qiran) and do not perform Tamattu'.' The crier announced, and as he passed by al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, he said: 'You will surely find among the young men a man who will reject what you say.' When the crier reached Ali (peace be upon him), who was at his camels feeding them with fodder and flour, upon hearing the announcement, he left them and went to Uthman and said: 'What is this that you have ordered?' He said: 'A opinion I have seen.' He said: 'By Allah, you have ordered contrary to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Then he turned away, raising his voice: 'Here I am with Hajj and Umrah together, here I am.' And Marwan ibn al-Hakam (may Allah curse him) said after that: 'As if I am looking at the whiteness of the flour mixed with the greenness of the fodder on his forearms.'

key_terms.الْأَبْوَاءِ: Al-Abwa', a place near Mecca where the Prophet performed Umrah
key_terms.تَمَتَّعُوا: To perform Tamattu' Hajj (separate Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Here I am (response to God's call)
key_terms.مَرْوَانُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ: Marwan ibn al-Hakam, a companion and later Umayyad caliph

ai.seo_question: What did Ali (AS) say when Uthman changed the Hajj ritual to Qiran?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential dispute between Caliph Uthman and Imam Ali (AS) regarding the form of Hajj, specifically contrasting Uthman's imposition of Qiran with Ali's adherence to the Prophet's Sunnah of Tamattu'. The narrative underscores Ali's public defiance and scholarly authority, using the vivid detail of flour on his arms to emphasize his active, practical engagement with the pilgrims during this critical moment of religious deviation.
